tests.procedure: BP stepwise solubility: 100 mg powdered sample in a stoppered tube + 0.1 mL solvent, then +0.9 mL, +2 mL, +7 mL; then 10 mg / 1 mg in 10 mL; shake 1 min then 15 min at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C at each step. Specification freely soluble in water.

details.steps: 100 mg + 0.1 mL (very soluble); + 0.9 mL (freely soluble); + 2 mL (soluble); + 7 mL (sparingly soluble); 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble); 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble); else practically insoluble
details.reference: BP (SC IV K) Characters Section in Monographs

tests.procedure: Dissolve 0.1 g in 2 mL water; add 2 mL of 150 g/L potassium carbonate; heat to boiling (no precipitate); add 4 mL potassium pyroantimonate solution; heat to boiling; cool in iced water, rubbing the inside of the tube with a glass rod if necessary. Dense white precipitate expected. (Test B, referring to the assay, is not on the spec sheet, see openQuestions.)

details.reference: BP Appendix VI Qualitative Reactions and Tests, Sodium
details.reagent: Potassium pyroantimonate solution: 2.0 g potassium pyroantimonate R in 100 mL hot water, boil about 5 min, cool quickly, add 10 mL of 150 g/L potassium hydroxide, stand 24 h, filter

tests.procedure: Heavy metals limit test (visual, lead standard). Sample: 1 g in a crucible, wet with sulfuric acid, char at low temperature, add 2 mL nitric acid and 5 drops sulfuric acid, heat until white fumes stop, ignite (preferably muffle furnace) at 500 to 600 until carbon burned off, cool, add 4 mL 6 N hydrochloric acid, cover, digest on steam bath 15 min, uncover, evaporate to dryness, moisten residue with 1 drop HCl, add 10 mL hot water, digest 2 min, add 6 N ammonium hydroxide dropwise until just alkaline to litmus, dilute to 25 mL, adjust with 1 N acetic acid to pH 3.0-4.0 (short-range indicator paper), filter if necessary, rinse crucible and filter with 10 mL water, combine in a 50 mL colour-comparison tube, dilute to 40 mL, mix. Standard: dilute 1.0 mL Stock Lead Standard Solution 1000 ppm to 100.0 mL with water (1 mL = 10 µg lead). To each tube (standard and test) add 2 mL pH 3.5 acetate buffer and 1.2 mL thioacetamide-glycerin base TS (or 3 drops sodium sulfide solution), dilute to 50 mL, mix, stand 2 min, view downward over a white surface; test not darker than standard.

details.equipment: Muffle furnace, steam bath, 50 mL colour-comparison tubes
details.standard: 1.0 mL Stock Lead Standard Solution 1000 ppm diluted to 100.0 mL with water; 1 mL = 10 µg lead

reagents.1 N acetic acid: 12 g glacial acetic acid to 100 mL with water
reagents.6 N hydrochloric acid: 50.0 mL hydrochloric acid to 100.0 mL with water
reagents.6M ammonium hydroxide: 33 mL concentrated ammonia to 100 mL with water
reagents.7M hydrochloric acid: 58.3 mL hydrochloric acid to 100.0 mL with water
reagents.2M hydrochloric acid: 206.0 g hydrochloric acid to 1000.0 mL with water
reagents.acetate buffer pH 3.5: 25 g ammonium acetate in 25 mL water + 38 mL 7M HCl, adjust to pH 3.5 with 2M HCl or 6M ammonia, dilute to 100 mL
reagents.thioacetamide-glycerin base TS: 0.2 mL thioacetamide solution + 1 mL of a mixture of 5 mL water, 15 mL 1 M NaOH and 20 mL glycerol (85 per cent); heat in water bath 20 s
reagents.1 M sodium hydroxide: 4.2 g NaOH to 100.0 mL with water
reagents.sodium sulfide solution: 5 g sodium sulfide in 10 mL water + 30 mL glycerol; 5 g NaOH in 30 mL water + 90 mL glycerol; divide into 2 equal portions, saturate with cooling, mix the 2 portions (text as written)

tests.procedure: Dry a weighing bottle at 105 °C and cool in a desiccator (W0). Weigh accurately 1.000 g into it (W1 = bottle + material). Dry in a calibrated oven at 105 °C for 2 h, cool in a desiccator, weigh (W2). Repeat to constant weight. % LOD = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.
tests.source: Sodium Selenate Anhydrous__STM Sodium Selenate Anhydrous.txt:35

tests.procedure: Flame AAS assay of selenium (one procedure stated for the three Se spec rows: total selenium, Se as selenate, Se as selenite). Standard: 5 mL of Selenium standard solution (1000 mg/L) to 50 mL with water (100 ppm). Sample: accurately weigh 23.95 mg of sample (equivalent to 10 mg selenium) into a 100 mL volumetric flask, complete to volume with water, sonicate 10 min. Measure by AAS (calibration graph from the standard as above).

details.technique: AAS (flame); treated as an ICP-type method per README rule 6
details.lamp: Hollow cathode Se, lamp current 10 mA
details.standardLevels: single level: Selenium standard solution 1000 mg/L, 5 mL to 50 mL with water = 100 ppm Se
details.standardPreparation: 5 mL Selenium standard solution (1000 mg/L) into a 50 mL volumetric flask, complete to volume with water (100 ppm)
details.samplePreparation: 23.95 mg of sample (equivalent to 10 mg Se) into 100 mL volumetric flask, water to volume, sonicate 10 min (about 100 ppm Se)
details.calculation: Assay as selenate % = (Abs test / Abs standard) x (Act.Wt.test / Theo.Wt.test) x (100 / (100 - MC)) x 100; Assay as selenium % = Assay as selenate % x (78.9 / 188.94)
details.calculationLegend: Abs test: absorbance of test solution at the same concentration of standard; Abs standard: absorbance of specific concentration of standard; Act.Wt.test: weight taken actually; Theo.Wt.test: weight to be taken; MC: moisture content of sample; At.wt Se 78.9 g/mol; M.wt sodium selenate 188.94 g/mol
details.reference: Analytical method validation for sodium selenate anhydrous

openQuestions.question: Only one AAS procedure is given (selenium as selenate, converted to selenium by 78.9/188.94). The STM has no procedure for Se as Selenite (NMT 1.0 %) or for how Se as Selenate (NLT 99.0 %) differs from the total; no speciation step is described. No rows' calculations beyond total selenium can be transcribed.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Selenate Anhydrous__STM Sodium Selenate Anhydrous.txt:36; Sodium Selenate Anhydrous__Specifications sheet Sodium Selenate Anhydrous.txt:17-19

openQuestions.question: Basis of the Se result rows is not stated (spec says only '%'). The formula divides by (100-MC) with MC 'moisture content of sample' (dried basis), but no such basis is on the spec sheet. Also unclear what the denominator of 'Se as Selenate %' and 'Se as Selenite %' is (percent of total selenium?). resultBasis left null.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Selenate Anhydrous__STM Sodium Selenate Anhydrous.txt:36; Sodium Selenate Anhydrous__Specifications sheet Sodium Selenate Anhydrous.txt:17-19

openQuestions.question: Assay formula: standard and sample are both prepared at about 100 ppm Se, yet the first result is called 'Assay as Selenate %' and is then multiplied by 78.9/188.94 to give 'Assay as Selenium %'. Which of the two is reported as Total Selenium (40.9-42.6 %)? Also only one standard level is given while the text says 'Calibration graph'.
openQuestions.source: Sodium Selenate Anhydrous__STM Sodium Selenate Anhydrous.txt:36

openQuestions.question: Identification Test B is 'described below in test of Assay', specification 'Comply', but the spec sheet lists only Reaction of Sodium. No row created; is Test B (AAS Se response) a required identification test?
